discussion_comments.comment_body: i tried it. taskbar icon persists as midnight no matter what i pick. tried restarting the app - still the default.
Hmm, that's weird, works for me...

Confirmed. Windows owns the pinned taskbar and task-group icon through the installed shortcut, so the runtime `WM_SETICON` override could not make this reliable across Windows configurations. I removed that unsupported path and its duplicate ICO resources. The picker now promises the supported Windows surface—the System tray—while the running window and Alt+Tab icon still update through Tauri.

The callback does discard the second launch's cwd, and a launch-derived workspace exists as a last-resort fallback when no remembered workspace validates. That does not amount to a supported "launch from a project to open it" flow: no entry point launches the app from a project directory, and Start, taskbar and Finder launches carry the install directory. Linux publishing is still pending in #14158.

Repeat launches activating the running instance is the intended behavior on every platform. Dev, beta and nightly builds have their own bundle identifiers, so they are unaffected. Forwarding argv or cwd belongs with a future "open this path" entry point. The shell also compiles on macOS with this change (`cargo check --locked`, plugin present in the dependency graph).

I don't think the P1 or Windows-only gating is warranted.
